verses.1: So, when Jesus heard that the Pharisees said that Jesus was creating more disciples and baptizing them than John had done—
verses.2: Although Jesus himself did not baptize, it was his disciples who did so.
verses.3: He left Judea and went back to Galilee once more.
verses.4: He must also pass through Samaria.
verses.5: So, he comes to the city of Samaria, called Siquah. It’s a place that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.
verses.6: There was a spring of Jacob’s. Jesus, who had stopped from his journey, sat down by that spring. It was the sixth hour of the day.
verses.7: A woman from Samaria comes to draw water. Jesus says to her, “Give me some water to drink.”
verses.8: For his disciples had gone into the town in order to buy food.
verses.9: So, the Samaritan woman said to him, “How can you, a Jew, ask questions of a Samaritan woman? After all, Jews and Samaritans are not compatible with each other.”
verses.10: Jesus replied to her, “If you know the gift of God, then who is it that says to you, ‘Give me water to drink’? You would have known him and given him life-giving water.”
verses.11: The woman said to him, “Lord, you have neither strength nor courage. Where does you get the water to live from?”
verses.12: Do not make yourself greater than our father Jacob. He gave us the bread, and he himself and his sons also shared it with us.
verses.13: Jesus replied to her, “Everyone who drinks from this water will thirst again.”
verses.14: And whoever drinks from the water that I give him, will not die in the time of drought. Instead, the water that I give him will become a source of eternal life for him.
verses.15: The woman said to him, “Lord, give me this water, so that I won’t drown or get trapped here.”
verses.16: He said to her, “Speak to your man, and come here.”
verses.17: The woman replied to him, “I have no husband.” Jesus said to her, “You are right to say that you have no husband.”
verses.18: For you have five men now, but the man that you have now isn’t really a man at all. This is what I truly mean.
verses.19: The woman said to him, “Lord, I think you are indeed a prophet.”
verses.20: Our fathers worshipped in this mountain. And you say that Jerusalem is the place where one should worship.
verses.21: Jesus said to her, “Believe me, woman, I tell you, it will come a time when neither in this mountain nor in Jerusalem will you worship your Father.”
verses.22: You worship what you do not know; we worship what we do know—that salvation comes from the Jews.
verses.23: But now comes the time when the true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth. For the Father indeed seeks such people who worship Him.
verses.24: The Spirit of God; those who worship Him must also worship Him in the Spirit and in truth.
verses.25: The woman said to him, “I know that Messias is coming. He is the one who will be called the Christ. When he comes, he will tell us everything.”
verses.26: Jesus said to her, “I am he who is speaking to you.”
verses.27: And in this manner, his disciples also came to see him. They were amazed that he could speak with a woman. But no one said anything. “What do you want?” or “What are you saying with her?”
verses.28: So, the woman took her water back with her. She went into the city and told the people about it.
verses.29: Now, see this man who told me everything I’ve done. Isn’t this the Christ?
verses.30: We came out of the city and went towards him.
verses.31: Among the disciples, those who were around him said to him, “Rabbi, eat.”
verses.32: And he said to them, “I will find something to eat for you. You don’t know what it is.”
verses.33: So, the disciples said to each other: “Shouldn’t anyone be assigned to feed him?”
verses.34: Jesus says to them, “I have a task to perform, so that I may fulfill the commandment given to me and complete his work.”
verses.35: Don’t you say that Etichotetramenos is also involved in this process? I tell you, open your eyes and look at the areas around you; they are white, and therefore suitable for this process.
verses.36: The one who collects wages also gathers fruits for a life of eternity, so that both the worker and the employer can rejoice together.
verses.37: For in this case, it is true that there is a difference between those who sow and those who reap.
verses.38: I have sent you out to punish those who did not deserve punishment. Others also deserved punishment, and you were dragged into their punishment.
verses.39: Many people from that city believed in him because of the testimony given by the woman who said, “She told me everything I’ve done.”
verses.40: So, when the Samaritans came to him, they asked him to stay with them. He stayed there for two days.
verses.41: And many others believed because of his words.
verses.42: To the woman, they said that we no longer would believe her words. For we had heard her say those things, and we knew that she truly was the savior of the world.
verses.43: After those two days, he went there to Galilee.
verses.44: For Jesus himself testified that he did not deserve to be honored as a prophet in his own homeland.
verses.45: When he arrived in Galilee, the people of Galilee welcomed him. They saw everything he did during the feast in Jerusalem. After all, they themselves also went to the feast.
verses.46: So, he went again to the region of Galilee, where he produced water that could be turned into wine. There was also a royal official whose son became sick in Kafarnaum.
verses.47: When he heard that Jesus had left Judea and gone to Galilee, he asked if he could go up with him and be baptized in his presence, as he was about to die.
verses.48: Then Jesus said to him, “If you see no signs or miracles, do not believe.”
verses.49: The royal official said to him, “My lord, please take my child away from me before he dies.”
verses.50: Jesus said to him, “Go. Your son lives.” The man believed in what Jesus said and went away.
verses.51: And as soon as he reached there, his servants came to him and said that the boy was alive.
verses.52: So, they decided to create a more beautiful world for them. They said to him that Echthes had been destroyed by the fire.
verses.53: So the father knew that in that hour, Jesus had said to him, “Your son lives.” And he and his entire household believed in it.
verses.54: Once again, Jesus made a second sign when he went from Judea to Galilee.
